 singapore MPA deploys spill response resources after sightings of oil patches near Semakau landfill
 Where necessary, relevant agencies will take precautionary measures to protect the shorelines MPA has activated its oil spill response contractors. Terminals in the area have also been directed to deploy their spill response resources. PHOTO: AsiaOne/Ong Chin Wee PUBLISHED ON November 01, 2026 8:30 AM BY Sean Ler The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) has activated its oil spill response contractors after several patches of oil were sighted off Pulau Sebarok, Pulau Semakau and Selat Pauh.
 The affected islands and waterway are between Pulau Bukom and Sentosa.
 In a news release on Sunday (Nov 1) afternoon, MPA said it was alerted to a sighting of oil in waters off Pulau Sebarok, to the east of Semakau landfill.
 Its aerial surveillance subsequently confirmed several patches of oil off Pulau Sebarok, Pulau Semakau and Selat Pauh.
 There were no sightings of oil patches near West Coast, Sentosa, Southern Islands and East Coast.
 The authority said it has activated its oil response contractors and terminals in the area have also been directed to deploy their spill response resources.
 Meanwhile, relevant agencies have been alerted to take precautionary measures to protect the shorelines, if necessary, while ships in port have also been asked to report any sightings of oil patches.
 Other agencies in the country's oil spill response operations typically include: the National Environment Agency, the National Parks Board, Sentosa Development Corporation, and Singapore Food Authority.
 There is presently no impact to navigation traffic and port operations, the authority said.
 "MPA is continuing with surveillance, working with agencies and terminals to mitigate and clean up the oil patches, and investigating the source of the oil," it added.
